failure_map_note: Full (unstaged) evaluation of all 1,185,408 voltage-compatible combinations; a build is counted under every check it fails. voltage_match cannot fail inside this population by construction, and grade_battery_c records zero failures on this catalog (structurally slack: the grade point's C-rate stays under every pack's limit), so both are omitted from the map.
naive_trap_definition: Datasheet-naive evaluation (the v1/v2 receipts' definition): peak (nameplate) torque for sustained checks, constant eta 0.92, aux fixed 0.4 kW (cooling draw ignored), tire load gross/4 vs nominal rating, raw Crr, single-point 50 km/h cruise range with no C-rate derating, static cooling heat comparisons. It accepts 308,401 builds on this catalog; 308,393 are rejected by the v3 verifier (the remaining 8 are the valid builds).

oracle_runtime.note: A naive unstaged exhaustive search over the raw catalog would take ~1.9 hours; the staged oracle is bounded by the full staged pass (~37 s).

physics_version: v3 (stateful thermal + SoC route simulation, towing load case)
prior_version_outcome: v2 (stateless) was solved by GLM-5.3 in 8m13s by faithful transcription + exhaustive search. Its winning build fails v3 on budget and towing grade_torque; the build gpt-oss submitted against v2 fails v3 on 5 checks.

staged_note: First failing stage per build under the oracle's staged evaluation order; only builds passing every stateless stage reach the route simulation.
trap_investigation: Post-lock: the brief's literal v2-physics trap definition measured 0 (see v2_physics_trap_note); two repair rounds reached 774 / 1,303 traps at the cost of the valid count (80 / 19, second round V144-only); the catalog was reverted to the locked md5 and re-verified (8 valids, staged histogram identical), and the datasheet-naive count (308,393) was measured with the v1/v2 receipts' naive definition.
tuning_path: Round 0 (budget $15,190, v2 parts rescaled + 4 new parts): exactly 1 valid build; the route sim's energy checks (soc_floor/range) formed the wall — 1,990 of 1,992 sim-reachers failed soc_floor.

Near-miss analysis: the V144 islands died on towing grade torque; the V96 family had NO path (best gearing failed towing grade torque by 24.7%, the high-ratio alternative failed top_speed_rpm) — a gearing scissors created by the towing case.
Round 1: BT-6 enlarged 43.5 -> 45.0 kWh, MT-5 continuous torque 148 -> 162 Nm, new V96 motor MT-8 authored strong: overshot to 94 valid builds (V96 22 / V144 72) with sub-0.15% knife-edge margins.

Round 2: MT-5 trimmed to 154, MT-8 to 164 Nm / 9000 rpm: both new islands collapsed; 20 valids, all MT-6 — trims re-opened halfway in round 3 (MT-5 158, MT-8 168/9300, BT-6 44.2 kWh): 28 valids, correct diversity skeleton.
Round 4: HD suspensions made honestly heavier (SU-2/3/5/6 +4..6 kg) to discipline near-free suspension swaps, MT-8 166, MT-5 157: 15 valids.

Final lock: MT-5 max_rpm 9500 -> 9560 (its sole surviving build was rpm-limited at exactly 125 km/h; it now achieves 126 with a 0.8% margin) and budget re-locked $15,190 -> $14,200: exactly 8 valid builds, tightest winning margin 0.20% (budget), both voltage families, 3 motors, 2 batteries, 2 chassis.
v2_physics_trap_note: Measured with the literal v2 physics evaluator (its own 16 checks, stateless, solo-only): it accepts ZERO builds on this catalog. All 8 v3 winners fail its static cooling pair (they run the 2.6 kW CL-1 radiator, which the v3 transient sim legitimizes but the static grade-point heat comparison rejects), and only 673 builds pass every other v2 check (the range wall shared by both models rejects 94.3%). Two re-calibration rounds aimed at the literal definition reached only 774 and 1,303 v2-accepted traps while destabilizing the v3 valid count (8 -> 80 -> 19); the towing gate leaks ~6% of any fattened stateless region into v3 validity, so >=100,000 literal v2-physics traps are structurally incompatible with 3-8 v3 valid builds on this catalog family. The locked calibration was restored unchanged.
